free_tier.stated: $50 of credits per organisation, unlimited sandboxes on the user's own machines at no charge, up to 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes and 3 active users a month.

egress.terms: not published: the pricing page prices hosted compute, memory and storage per hour and lists no egress allowance or per-GB overage

record.interface_detail: SSH, the CLI and the API; a TypeScript SDK (@amika/sdk) and a web UI also exist

limits.value: 3 active users a month on Free and 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes
past 3 active users the whole organisation moves to Team at $30 an active user a month

identity_cost.detail: an email address and a name at sign-up: the join form asks 'First name Last name Email Continue' and offers 'Continue with Google' or GitHub in place of the email, and it carries no phone field. Whether a payment method is asked for while the free plan's credits are claimed is unverified: behind a sign-up; neither the join page nor https://www.amika.dev/pricing publishes one.

record.confidence_note: the pricing page was read on 2026-10-22. The free grant is USD 50 of credits, and the important half is that hours on the user's own machines are never charged on any plan, which makes the hosted credit a convenience rather than the capacity.

evidence.proved: '$50 of credits per organization to start' and 'Unlimited sandboxes on any number of your own machines' and 'Up to 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes' and 'Free allows 3 a month' active users, and 'Sandboxes there run on every plan and their hours are never charged', quoted
the Free plan lists SSH, the CLI and the API as ways to connect
evidence.quote: Connect from Cursor, Codex, SSH, the CLI, or the API

record.notes: The free tier includes USD 50 of credits and up to 10 concurrent service-account sandboxes, which the vendor meters; the unlimited sandboxes run on machines the user supplies.

session_cap.note: hosted sandboxes bill per second; hours on a user's own machines are never charged and have no clock
